Expectation1: Maintain regular communication with family members
Situation1: A family holiday is approaching, which is a traditional time for everyone to reconnect.
Expectation2: Attend weekly church services to worship and participate in community activities
Situation2: They recognize the importance of being present at weekly services regularly
Story: The calendar on my kitchen wall is marked with two bright circles: one for the upcoming family holiday, and one for Sunday’s church service. As a grandparent, I know how much my children and grandchildren look forward to our holiday gatherings. It’s the one time we all sit around the same table, sharing stories and laughter, and I’m expected to be the glue that keeps us connected. But this year, the holiday falls on the same weekend as a special church service I’ve committed to attend. My church family relies on me, too—I help with the choir and lead a prayer group, and my absence would be noticed. I feel the weight of both worlds pressing in. My daughter calls, her voice warm with anticipation, “We can’t wait to see you, Mom.” Later, my pastor reminds me, “Your presence uplifts us all.” I pace the living room, torn between the joy of family and the peace I find in worship. My heart aches, knowing I can’t be in two places at once, and I wonder which part of me I’ll have to disappoint.
